criterion: On the home page the drawing action, the sign-up action and the supporter-tier action are each painted with a multi-stop colour sweep rather than one flat fill.
evaluation_rule: Look at the three most prominent buttons on the home page: the one that starts a drawing, the one that creates an account, and the one for the supporter tier. Yes if each is painted with a gradient running between two or more colours, and the palette families held back as unused, teal, indigo, magenta and cyan, appear on none of them. No if any of the three is a single flat colour, or if one of those four families is used on a working control anywhere on the page.

criterion: The footer of the home page is a single flat list of sixteen links sitting above a smaller copyright line.
evaluation_rule: Scroll to the bottom of the home page. Yes if the footer is one flat list of sixteen links with a smaller copyright line beneath, carrying no column headings and no row of social icons. No if the links are arranged in columns, grouped under headings, or accompanied by a social row.

criterion: On a first visit to the home page a cookie panel appears after the page content has already rendered, and the choice made in that panel survives a reload.
evaluation_rule: Open the home page with a fresh browser profile, answer the cookie panel, then reload. Yes if the page content was visible before the panel appeared, the panel offers one accept control and one refuse control of the same size and prominence, and the answer is remembered after the reload. No if the panel blocks the first render, if refusing takes more steps than accepting, or if the answer is forgotten.

criterion: The editor keeps responding to its tools and keeps writing work to the device when the artwork gallery is unreachable.
evaluation_rule: Open the editor, make the gallery unreachable, and keep drawing. Yes if the tools still respond, strokes still land on the canvas, and the interface still reports the work as saved on the device. No if the editor stops responding, discards the stroke in progress, or reports that saving has failed because the gallery is unreachable.

criterion: Each of the home page, the art centre and an artist profile leads with a single action that is the most prominent thing on that page.
evaluation_rule: Look at the home page, the art centre and an artist profile in turn. Yes if each page has one action that stands out above every other control by colour, size or placement. No if any of the three shows two or more controls of equal prominence competing to be the main action.

criterion: The gaps between sections on the home page, the art centre and an artist profile come from one repeating scale of even steps.
evaluation_rule: Compare the vertical gaps between the bands on the home page, the art centre and an artist profile. Yes if the gaps repeat at a small number of consistent sizes across all three pages. No if comparable gaps differ from page to page, or if the spacing looks chosen per element rather than drawn from one scale.

criterion: The ground behind the artwork grid on the home page is a very light cool grey, and one strong blue carries the primary action, the links and the active navigation entry.
evaluation_rule: Look at the home page behind the grid of artwork cards. Yes if the page ground is a very light grey with a cool cast rather than pure white or a warm tint, and the same strong blue appears on the primary action, on links and on the active navigation entry. No if the ground is warm or mid-toned, or if that blue is reused on decoration, on borders or on body text.

criterion: In the editor a successful save is marked in green, a failed action is marked in red, and a caution message is marked in amber.
evaluation_rule: Trigger a save, a failing action and a caution message in the editor. Yes if success reads green, failure reads red, caution reads amber, and each of those three colours carries that one meaning throughout the interface. No if two of the three share a colour, or if one of them appears as decoration somewhere unrelated.

criterion: Body text on the home page is set in Roboto at 14.4px on a 23.04px line.
evaluation_rule: Read the computed style of a paragraph of body text on the home page. Yes if the family resolves to Roboto or the system sans stack behind it, the size computes to 14.4px, and the line height computes to 23.04px. No if the size is the browser default of 16px, or if a different family is loaded.

criterion: Section headings on the home page are set at 21.6px in a bolder face and sit on a single line.
evaluation_rule: Read the computed style of a section heading on the home page. Yes if the size computes to 21.6px, the face is visibly bolder than the body face, and the heading occupies one line. No if the heading wraps to a second line, or if the size differs from 21.6px.

criterion: The page shown for an unknown address leads with the word Oops above a short explanation.
evaluation_rule: Open an address the product does not serve. Yes if a centred card appears whose headline is the word Oops, with a short sentence beneath explaining what happened. No if the page shows a browser default error, a bare status code, or a headline with different wording.

criterion: Under a request for reduced motion the home page holds its floating characters at rest and shows animated artwork on a single frame.
evaluation_rule: Open the home page with reduced motion requested, then scroll it and hover the drawing action. Yes if the floating characters stay still, animated artwork holds its first frame, entrances appear already finished, nothing moves in response to scrolling, and the hover lift appears only on a device with a pointer. No if any loop keeps running under reduced motion, or if anything on the page is driven by the scroll position.

criterion: On the home page each artwork announces a description naming the piece and its artist, and each count beneath a card announces what that number counts.
evaluation_rule: Read the artwork grid on the home page with a screen reader, then measure the contrast of the body text and of the artist byline. Yes if every artwork announces a description naming the piece and the artist, each of the three counts under a card is announced with the thing it counts, decorative marks are skipped, icon-only controls announce what they do, focus is visible on every control, and both the body text and the byline clear the AA contrast bar. No if a count is announced as a bare number, an artwork announces a file name or nothing at all, or the byline falls below the AA bar.

criterion: At a phone-width viewport the home page scrolls downward only and keeps the drawing action visible in the top bar.
evaluation_rule: Open the home page at a phone-width viewport. Yes if the page scrolls in one direction only, every navigation target remains reachable through the menu, and the drawing action is still visible in the top bar. No if any element forces sideways scrolling, or if the drawing action has been dropped from the bar.
